title: Changes of state

match.reason: The closest bank point covers the particle explanation of melting, freezing, boiling and condensing, but it does not teach that temperature stays level on a heating graph during a state change, which the brief requires, and it does not name evaporating, so matching it would need a new idea rather than a small change.

draft.title: Changes of state
card: Melting (solid to liquid), evaporating or boiling (liquid to gas) happen when particles gain energy. Particles move faster and break free from their neighbours.
Condensing (gas to liquid) and freezing (liquid to solid) happen when particles lose energy. They slow down and pull closer together.
Evaporation happens at the surface of a liquid at many temperatures. Boiling happens throughout the liquid at its boiling point.
On a heating graph, the temperature stays level while a substance changes state. The energy added is used to separate particles, not to speed them up.

4.alt: A heating graph of temperature against time. The line rises, goes flat during melting, rises again, goes flat during boiling, then rises again.

draft.remember: Gaining energy lets particles move apart. Losing energy lets them move closer.

a.q: Steam from a kettle touches a cold window and turns into drops of water. What happens to the particles?
opts: They lose energy and move closer together
They gain energy and move closer together
They lose energy and move further apart
They gain energy and move further apart
a.why: Condensing is a gas changing to a liquid. The particles lose energy, slow down and move closer. Gaining energy would make them move apart, as in boiling.
a.clue: Cooling takes energy away from the particles.

b.q: Sam heats ice and records its temperature. While the ice is melting, the thermometer reading stays at 0 °C. What explains this?
opts: The energy added is used to separate particles
The ice has stopped gaining any energy
The particles are vibrating faster and faster
The heater is not warm enough to heat ice
b.why: During a change of state, the added energy is used to pull particles apart, so the temperature stays level. The ice is still gaining energy, so the second option is wrong.
b.clue: Think about where the added energy goes during melting.

a.best: They lose energy and move closer together

b.best: The energy added is used to separate particles

proposal.title: Changes of state
card: Melting (solid to liquid), evaporating and boiling (liquid to gas) happen when particles gain energy. As a substance heats up, its particles speed up. During the change of state, the energy breaks them free from their neighbours.
Condensing (gas to liquid) and freezing (liquid to solid) happen when particles lose energy. As a substance cools, its particles slow down. During the change of state, they pull closer together.
Evaporation happens at the surface of a liquid at many temperatures. Boiling happens throughout the liquid at its boiling point.
On a heating graph, the temperature stays level while a substance changes state. The energy added is used to separate particles, not to speed them up.

opts: They lose energy and move closer together

a.why: Condensing is a gas changing to a liquid. The particles lose energy to the cold window and pull closer together. Gaining energy would make them move apart, as in boiling.
a.clue: The cold window takes energy away from the particles.

b.q: Sam heats ice and records its temperature. While the ice is melting, the thermometer reading stays at 0 °C. What explains this?
opts: The energy added is used to separate particles

b.why: During a change of state, the added energy is used to pull particles apart rather than speed them up, so the temperature stays level. The ice is still gaining energy, so the second option is wrong. If the particles were speeding up, the temperature would rise.
